Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0099", "row_sha256": "b773ed150b26d67fb5a82a9a32e80325bdb6ee8aa01683a1ec220172aa22fc9b", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "we need a prompt for a replacement sign at the Morrow Creek Trail junction, and the draft should be for Tess, not Idris. the old one is at the east fork, 2.4 miles from the North Gate parking lot and about 0.3 miles past the footbridge. people arrive there and then choose a route, so this is a decision point, not a general trailhead sign. Please ask for replacement sign text and a short layout note, not for a whole trail guide or a work plan. I'm trying to get the request in one place because the notes came from different walks and a couple of conversations.

The sign is a wooden panel, 24 by 18 inches, attached to a post. The lettering has faded after repeated rain, and the panel is warped, but the post is still sound. The crew expects to replace the panel and keep the existing post; don't make the prompt sound as if both need replacing. Ranger Mina said, “The post is sound; the panel has taken the weather.” That quote can be included as background for the person drafting the sign, but it is not sign wording. We don't have a replacement date, and none needs to be supplied. The request should keep the repair scope to the panel and say why a new panel is needed without implying that the junction itself is closed.

For the routes, the left-hand choice is Hemlock Loop, 1.7 miles back to the North Gate parking lot. The right-hand choice is the Raven Shelf Overlook spur, 0.6 mile to the overlook. The last 0.2 mile of that spur is steep and has loose gravel. It should be possible to make the warning clear but not dramatic. There is also the Morrow Creek Trail continuing straight from the junction for 3.2 miles to the south boundary. The sign needs to make the directions and names easy to tell apart, especially left, right, and straight, since people are reading it before they set off. Please don't switch the route distances or make them sound like distances from the parking lot when they refer to the junction.

One complication is that people sometimes treat the whole area as one trail, so the replacement should show that Hemlock Loop, Raven Shelf Overlook spur, and the continuing Morrow Creek Trail are separate choices from this point. The old board gave the route names but the faded arrows are hard to read now. We haven't got a newer map, a color scheme, or a standard arrow design to copy, so don't claim that one is provided. The short layout note can say how to separate the three directional entries on the 24-by-18-inch panel, using only the directions already known. It should not add symbols, mileage markers along the routes, or other trail facts that aren't in these notes.

The intended audience is hikers who have reached the fork on foot. Keep the wording brief enough for an outdoor sign and make the main route choices scannable at a glance, rather than writing a paragraph that would be hard to read on the panel. Use the route names exactly as given, including “Raven Shelf Overlook” and “Morrow Creek Trail.” Include the warning about the steep, loose-gravel last section only with the overlook spur; don't accidentally make it sound like the whole Morrow Creek route has that surface. The North Gate parking lot is a destination named for Hemlock Loop, not another direction from the junction.

Can the prompt request a draft of the actual replacement sign wording and a short layout note for the panel? It should ask for clear directional wording, with each route paired with its correct direction and distance. For the Overlook entry, make the last 0.2 mile warning visible beside or below that route, while retaining the total 0.6-mile distance to the overlook. For Hemlock Loop, retain the 1.7-mile distance back to the lot. For Morrow Creek Trail, retain the straight-ahead direction and 3.2 miles to the south boundary. We do not need a separate route description, scenic copy, or history of the area; the purpose is helping a hiker choose correctly at this junction.

The new sign is being considered because faded lettering and a warped panel are hard to use in wet weather, even though the post can remain. Please keep that distinction if the prompt mentions the condition of the existing sign. It is okay to use the quote from Mina to explain the condition in the drafting brief, but don't put her quote on the finished sign or change it into a promise about the repair. There is no report here of a trail closure, a hazard beyond the described loose gravel, or a change to any route. Don't fill those gaps in. I only need the prompt organized so another writer can prepare the proposed text and layout note.

For the output requested inside that prompt, make it clear the writer is preparing a proposal, not claiming the new panel has already been installed. Have them present the sign wording distinctly from the short layout note so we can review what hikers would read separately from the explanation of how it could fit. It can be useful to list the three entries in an orderly way, with the direction first or the route name first, as long as the association stays unmistakable. The sign itself should not address Tess; Tess is who should receive the draft. The destination labels are not to be renamed or abbreviated.

There is no need to invent a date, material specification beyond the wooden panel we have, an approval, or a decision about the crew's schedule. The post is at the east fork as noted, the locations and distances are measured from the junction or along the named route as stated, and the rough condition description is all we have. Keep the request focused on a useful replacement for that particular panel. Please finish the prompt with the separate project detail that the crew plans to reuse the existing post, so that fact is easy to find without being confused with the wording hikers will see.", "output": "Prepare a draft replacement sign for Tess, not Idris, for the Morrow Creek Trail junction. Provide the proposed sign wording and a short layout note; do not write a trail guide or work plan. This is a decision point where hikers choose a route, not a general trailhead sign.

The existing sign is at the east fork, 2.4 miles from the North Gate parking lot and about 0.3 miles past the footbridge. It is a 24-by-18-inch wooden panel attached to a post. Repeated rain has faded the lettering and warped the panel, but the post is sound. Ranger Mina said, “The post is sound; the panel has taken the weather.” This quote is background only, not wording for the sign. The crew expects to replace the panel and reuse the existing post. No replacement date is available. Describe the need for a new panel without suggesting the junction is closed or that the post needs replacement.

### Information for the sign
Present the three routes as separate choices from the junction, with each name clearly paired with its direction and distance:

1. **Left:** Hemlock Loop — 1.7 miles back to the North Gate parking lot.
2. **Right:** Raven Shelf Overlook spur — 0.6 mile to the overlook. The last 0.2 mile is steep and has loose gravel; make this warning clear but not dramatic, and associate it only with this spur.
3. **Straight:** Morrow Creek Trail — 3.2 miles to the south boundary.

Keep the route names exactly as given, including “Raven Shelf Overlook” and “Morrow Creek Trail.” Do not change the distances or imply that they are all measured from the parking lot: they refer to the junction or named route as stated above. North Gate parking lot is the Hemlock Loop destination, not an additional direction from the junction. Make left, right, and straight easy to distinguish for hikers reading the sign before setting off.

### Draft and layout
Keep the sign wording brief, scannable at a glance, and suitable for an outdoor panel. Provide the actual proposed wording separately from the short layout note, so the text hikers would read is distinct from the explanation of how it could fit on the 24-by-18-inch panel. The layout note may explain how to separate the three directional entries using the directions provided. There is no newer map, color scheme, or standard arrow design to copy, so do not claim one is available or introduce unsupported trail facts, symbols, or mileage markers. The entries may put the direction or route name first, as long as each pairing remains unmistakable.

Do not add a separate route description, scenic copy, or area history. Do not invent a date, additional material specification, approval, crew schedule, trail closure, or route change. The only described route hazard is the steep, loose-gravel final 0.2 mile of the Raven Shelf Overlook spur. Do not imply that this condition applies to Morrow Creek Trail or the entire junction. The output is a proposal for review, not a claim that the replacement panel has been installed. Do not address Tess on the sign, rename or abbreviate any destination, or turn Mina’s quote into sign text or a promise about the repair.

The crew plans to reuse the existing post while replacing the wooden panel."}]
